[CA] Coworker has been clocking in with my employee number and now I'm the one getting written up

Location: San Jose, California. I work at a big box retail store (not gonna say which). We clock in on a tablet by typing our employee number and a 4 digit PIN. My number is ⟦employee id|40917⟧ and I stupidly let a coworker (I'll call her ⟦name|Dana⟧) watch me type my PIN back in June when the tablet was glitching.

Fast forward to now and there are 6 shifts on my record where I supposedly clocked in at 5:58am but I don't even work mornings. Our store manager ⟦name|Raymond⟧ pulled the camera footage for one of them and it's clearly ⟦name|Dana⟧ at the tablet, but he says "the system says it's you, so it's on you" and gave me a final written warning. HR (corporate, not in store) hasn't answered my email in 9 days.

Questions:
1. Can they actually discipline me for this when they have video of someone else?
2. Do I need to worry about this being called time theft? Those 6 shifts were paid out to MY number, about $410 total.
3. Should I just quit before they fire me?

Edit: I changed my PIN the same day I found out. And yes I know letting her see it was dumb.

---

u/⟦username|LawTalkingGuy_77⟧ · 5h
Don't quit. Write down everything now while it's fresh: dates of the 6 shifts, the date ⟦name|Raymond⟧ showed you the footage, the name of the HR person you emailed. Then send HR a second email that says plainly "the footage reviewed by the store manager on [date] shows another employee using my credentials." Get it in writing.

u/⟦username|throwaway_sjc_8812⟧ · 5h
Thank you. The HR person is ⟦name|Courtney Abiodun⟧, I'll cc her manager this time.

u/⟦username|retail_lifer_2009⟧ · 4h
Former ASM here. If the money went to your paycheck, offer in writing to pay it back. Shows good faith and kills the "time theft" angle dead.

Chapter 4: Restricted

Notes:
Sorry this took forever, I started a new job lol. Huge thanks to my beta ⟦name|Jess⟧ (⟦username|jesswritesthings⟧ on tumblr) who caught approximately 400 comma splices, and to my roommate ⟦name|Ana Lucía⟧ for listening to me read the library scene out loud at 2am.

The library was never truly empty, Hermione had learned, only quiet in different ways. At half past ten on a Tuesday it held Madam Pince's footsteps, the scratch of a single quill, and - tonight - Draco Malfoy, asleep on a copy of Advanced Rune Translation with ink on his cheek.

She considered leaving him. She considered, briefly and uncharitably, a Sticking Charm.

"You're staring, Granger," he said without opening his eyes.

"You're drooling on a library book. Madam Pince will have your head."

"Madam Pince," he said, sitting up and peeling a page off his face with as much dignity as the situation allowed, "adores me. I alphabetised the Restricted Section for her in September. Voluntarily."

"Under McGonagall's orders."

"Voluntarily under orders." He squinted at the clock. "Merlin. Is Longbottom still in the greenhouses?"

"Neville," Hermione said pointedly, "is in bed, like a sensible person."

"And yet here you are."

She sat down across from him before she could think better of it.

End Notes:
Next chapter: Ginny finds out. Come scream at me in the comments or on discord (⟦username|moonlitquill⟧). Kudos keep me alive!

Is putting 15% in my 401k + a Roth IRA overkill at 26 if I still have student loans?

Background: 26, $68,000 salary, employer matches 50% up to 6%. Student loans are $21,400 at 4.99% (federal, not on any forgiveness track). Emergency fund is $9,000 in a HYSA at 4.1%. No car payment, rent is $1,350.

Right now I'm doing 15% to the 401k and $500/mo to a Roth. That leaves me about $600/mo "extra" after everything. My dad keeps sending me Dave Ramsey clips telling me to stop investing and throw everything at the loans until they're gone. My coworker swears by the Warren Buffett "rule no. 1: never lose money" thing and keeps everything in an S&P 500 index fund.

Is there a right answer here or is this just vibes?

---

u/⟦username|IndexAndChill_⟧ · 1d · 312 points
At 4.99% it's basically a coin flip mathematically. You're getting the full match, which is the only non-negotiable part. Personally I'd drop the 401k to 10%, keep the Roth, and put the difference toward the loans so they're gone in about 3 years. Also check the wiki flowchart.

u/⟦username|budget_ferret⟧ · 1d
Thank you, this is actually really helpful. The flowchart puts me at step 5 so I guess I'm doing fine lol

u/⟦username|sallymae_survivor⟧ · 22h · 141 points
Ignore the Ramsey stuff for a 4.99% loan. That advice is built for people carrying 22% credit card balances.

The end of the world, it turned out, had terrible tea.

"It's not the tea's fault," the Doctor said, peering into her mug as though it might apologise. "It's the water. Recycled through about four hundred million years of planetary crust. Very mineral. Character-building."

Yaz took a sip and immediately regretted it. "It tastes like a radiator."

"A radiator with character."

Outside the viewing window the sun swelled, red and patient. Graham had gone off to find biscuits, which Yaz suspected was cover for a nap, and Ryan had his face pressed to the glass like a kid at an aquarium.

"Do you ever get tired of it?" Yaz asked. "Watching things end?"

The Doctor was quiet for long enough that Yaz thought she hadn't heard. Then she set the mug down, very carefully, the way you put down something you mean to come back to.

"I don't watch them end," she said. "I watch them happen. There's a difference. Mostly."
